title: RATE: a 116/116 error basin on the structural axis, exact bits still open
status_plain: RATE's schedule and substrate were identified -- forward-difference Newton in r-space, with the power computed by the x87 87tran exp-times-ln chain -- but exact bits remain open and no fix has landed. The one count RATE has is a #NUM! error basin, 116 of 116 across five corpora, and that is the structural-admission axis: it is error placement, not arithmetic. Its subject is genuinely unclear. The sentence sits inside the agent-R identification narrative, the row is M1, and nothing on the line says production-kernel replay -- which is exactly what the NPER and XNPV sign-offs do say. It is therefore recorded as attribution-unclear rather than resolved by plausibility. RATE's numeric side is not a figure at all: the source publishes an interval, exact bits 0-2 of 101, which cannot be parsed as passed over total and is recorded as a divergence with no numerator.
